newsitem.title: FINLAND: Niinisto sees no conflict with Finland Bank on ERM.
newsitem.headline: Niinisto sees no conflict with Finland Bank on ERM.

text.p: Finnish Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto was quoted as saying that there was no conflict between the Bank of Finland and the government on the issue of whether to link the markka to Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM).

"There is no conflict between the government and the Bank of Finland on this question," Niinisto was quoted as saying in Finance Finland, the quarterly newsletter of the Finnish Foundation for Share Promotion, received on Thursday.
Niinisto repeated that the decision whether to link the markka to ERM would be made "one way or the other during the autumn".
The linkage of the markka to ERM had become a hot topic of debate, the newsletter said. Resistance from the Bank of Finland was suspected of being a factor behind the decision's delay, it said.
In the interview, Niinisto said the markka had been stable.

"The Maastricht Treaty (formally) requires ERM linkage before EMU membership. However, final interpretation within the EU is still unclear in this respect. The fact is that the markka has stabilised at its present level during the period of its flotation," Niinisto was quoted as saying.
The markka was allowed to float freely in September 1992.
